images.title: Change the exponent, not the coefficient
images.purpose: Compares 2 × 10⁷ with 3 × 10⁷ and with 2 × 10 to the power 8 using bars drawn to scale.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. Three horizontal bars from one left edge, stacked top to bottom, the last one much longer.
images.exact_structure: Three horizontal bars with left ends aligned, lengths in the ratio 2 : 3 : 20. Bar 1, teal (#0072B2), labelled '2 × 10⁷' at its left and '2 crore' at its right end. Bar 2, amber (#E69F00), labelled '3 × 10⁷' and '3 crore'. Bar 3, reddish purple (#CC79A7), labelled '2 × 10⁸' and '20 crore'; it stretches across most of the frame. Exactly 3 bars.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Changing the exponent by 1 multiplies the number by 10; changing the coefficient changes it far less.
images.description: Compares 2 × 10⁷ with 3 × 10⁷ and with 2 × 10 to the power 8 using bars drawn to scale.
images.context: 2 × 10⁷ = 2 crore, 3 × 10⁷ = 3 crore, 2 × 10 to the power 8 = 20 crore. Kohima about 1.42 × 10 to the power 5.
images.teaching_notes: Link to precision: the digits of the coefficient show how well the number is known.

image_decisions.why: The three bars show at a glance that the exponent matters more than the coefficient.
